safety-orange.$description: Safety Orange — Brand accent — terminal periods after display headlines, thin underlines on key phrases, small icon accents, and full-bleed section bands. This is the only chromatic color in the system; it must be used sparingly, like a highlighter on a printed page

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

carbon.$description: Carbon — Heading text where pure black feels too harsh; gives display type a slightly softer, warmer read without losing the editorial weight

graphite.$description: Graphite — Body secondary text, nav inactive items, caption labels. The workhorse muted neutral for supporting copy and metadata

slate.$description: Slate — Lighter secondary text and subdued headings — used when Graphite would compete with body copy

fog.$description: Fog — Disabled state text, tertiary metadata, placeholder labels

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas and primary surface — the dominant background across all sections. Sits between pure white and cream to soften the high-contrast black typography

cream.$description: Cream — Warmest surface tint for elevated cards and feature blocks — barely a degree warmer than Paper, but enough to read as a distinct layer

ash.$description: Ash — Mid-tone surface for cards that need more separation from the Paper canvas without introducing a border

linen.$description: Linen — Warmest card surface variant — used for product mockup containers and illustration cards that need a tactile, paper-like feel

sans-serif.$description: sans-serif — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

bricolage-grotesque.$description: Primary display and heading font. Used for all headlines, section titles, and feature headings. The variable weight range (500–600) and aggressive negative tracking on large sizes create poster-like headline blocks that read as printed editorial type rather than web text. Tighter tracking at larger sizes is a signature choice — the letters almost touch, creating compact, confident word shapes.

geist.$description: UI and navigation typeface. Used for nav links, button labels, form text, table-of-contents entries, and interface chrome. The tighter tracking at 24px and near-normal at 14px makes it a comfortable workhorse for dense UI contexts where Bricolage Grotesque would feel too editorial.

geist-variable.$description: Secondary body and utility text at lighter weight. Used for fine print, metadata, timestamps, and supporting body copy where Geist 500/600 would feel too heavy.

inter.$description: Fallback body and link text. Used in contexts where Inter's broader availability matches the design intent without requiring a custom font load.
